newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA COLLECTS MORE WHEAT THAN LAST YEAR.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA COLLECTS MORE WHEAT THAN LAST YEAR.

text.p: Bulgaria has collected more than one million tonnes of wheat from this year's crop by last weekend compared to the same period last year, the agriculture ministry said on Tuesday.

"We have collected 2.95 million tonnes at average yield of 3.16 tonnes per hectare by August 8 against 1.76 million tonnes at average yield of 1.85 tonnes per hectare for the same period last year," a ministry spokeswoman told reporters.

Until Tuesday Bulgaria has collected a total of 3.14 million tonnes from 80 percent of the sown areas boosting average yield to 3.2 tonnes per hectare despite heavy rainfalls which have delayed the harvest, ministry figures show.
Ultimate wheat harvest deadline for Bulgaria is end-July. Some 240,000 hectares have not been harvested so far and everyday rainfalls affect the quality of the crop.
Bulgaria's annual consumption is estimated at 1.6 million tonnes of bread wheat and 800,000 tonnes of feed wheat.
Agriculture minister Ventsislav Varbanov said on Monday private and state mills have bought a total of 800,000 tonnes of wheat so far.

The minimum purchase price is set at 230,000 levs per tonne from this year's crop in a bid to secure the country's grain balance after excessive wheat exports two years ago and a bad harvest in 1996 caused acute grain shortages earlier this year.

The State Fund for Reconstruction and Development said last week it had placed guarantees worth 203 billion levs from planned 230 billion levs with banks which extend credits to state companies to fund purchasing of wheat.
Bulgaria has to export some 232,000 tonnes of wheat this year under futures contracts agreed earlier this year. Poland has said it could accept cash payment for 100,000 of the total.
An export fee of 15 percent of international wheat prices has been also set in a bid to curb exports.
